title: Parallel amide coupling in 96-well plates with automated fluorous solid-phase extraction
summary: Describes a 96-well parallel amide-coupling library using a fluorous triazine coupling reagent, workup through an ion-exchange resin plate, automated fluorous SPE, and Genevac evaporation, with LC-MS purity check. Useful for timing the coupling, workup and evaporation stages together.

steps.text: Set up 8 x 12 reactions in a 96-well plate at 0.05 mmol scale (acid plus fluorous triazine reagent and N-methylmorpholine) and shake 30 min at 25 C.
Add the amines and allow the coupling to run about 2 h.
Transfer mixtures to a plate holding silica-supported SAX resin and rinse with THF (about 0.75 mL) to remove acid and byproducts.
Concentrate the filtrates on a Genevac EZ-2 centrifugal evaporator.
Redissolve residues in 0.5-1 mL DMF and load onto an automated fluorous SPE system (conditioning, load, 90:10 DMF/water fluorophobic elution of non-fluorous product, THF cartridge wash).

duration_s.note: About 9 min per cartridge stated; up to ~100 separations in 1-2 h unattended.

steps.text: Evaporate the collected product fractions again on the Genevac and transfer to pre-weighed vials.
Check product purity by LC-MS with UV detection (87 of 96 products above 90% in the paper).

equipment.name: 96-well reaction plate and SAX resin plate

materials: Fluorous triazine coupling reagent, carboxylic acids, amines, NMM, THF, DMF
safety: Flammable solvents; evaporator and SPE in ventilated area.
